facts.text: Marlborough’s city seal, adopted in 1890, shows a factory, a shoe box, and a pair of boots, a nod to its shoe‑making past.
The Rockport Company, founded in Marlborough in 1971, operated an outlet store there until 2017, linking the town to a national footwear brand.
Frye boots were manufactured in Marlborough through the 1970s, making the town a key player in American boot production.
The Marlborough Historical Society, founded in 1964, is an all‑volunteer nonprofit that preserves local history and offers tours of the Peter Rice Homestead.
Marlborough transitioned from a 1660 town to a city in 1890, a change that paralleled the boom of its shoe industry.
The annual Horatio Alger Street Fair, renamed the Harvest Fair in 2007, honors the author who graduated from Marlborough High School in 1847.
